subtopic: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Alpha Particle Deflection
question: A positively charged particle (alpha particle) projected toward the West is deflected toward the North by a magnetic field. What is the direction of the magnetic field?
options: Towards the South
Towards the East
Downwards into the page
Upwards (out of the page)
explanation: Since the alpha particle has a positive charge, the direction of current is along its motion (West). The deflection force is towards the North. Applying Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: align middle finger (current) to West, thumb (force) to North. The forefinger (magnetic field) points vertically upwards (out of the page).
citation: NCERT Class 10 Science, Chapter 12, NCERT In-Text Question Section 12.3

subtopic: Electron Deflection in Magnetic Field
question: An electron moves vertically downwards into a horizontal magnetic field directed towards the East. In which direction is the mechanical force acting on the electron directed?
options: Towards the North
Vertically upwards
Towards the South
Towards the West
explanation: Use the magnetic Lorentz-force direction. For a positive charge moving downward, v × B with B toward the East points South. An electron has negative charge, so its force is in the opposite direction: North. Equivalently, conventional current is upward; applying Fleming’s left-hand rule with field East gives force North.

subtopic: Fuse Placement: Mandatory Live Wire Installation
question: Why must an electric fuse ALWAYS be connected in series with the LIVE wire and NEVER in the neutral wire?

Fuses can only conduct positive electric charges
If connected in the neutral wire, when the fuse blows due to a fault, the appliance remains connected to the 220 V live wire, presenting a lethal shock risk to anyone touching it

subtopic: Plug Standards: Three-Pin vs Two-Pin Classification
question: Why do many metal-bodied appliances use a three-pin plug with an earth pin, while an appropriately double-insulated plastic-cased appliance may use a two-pin plug?

The third pin is only used to charge batteries
Two-pin plugs prevent high electricity bills

Metal-bodied appliances with accessible conductive enclosures need protective earthing; appropriately double-insulated appliances are designed so accessible parts cannot become live under a single insulation fault
explanation: A protective earth conductor bonds an accessible conductive enclosure to the installation’s earthing system, providing a low-impedance fault path so the protective device can disconnect the supply. question: A stationary alpha particle (charge +2e, velocity v = 0) is placed inside an extremely powerful 10 Tesla uniform magnetic field. What is the magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the alpha particle?

20 Newtons
3.2 * 10^-18 Newtons
Infinite force
explanation: Magnetic force on a charged particle is given by Lorentz magnetic force F = q * v * B * sin(theta). A magnetic field only exerts force on MOVING charges (v > 0). Because the particle is stationary (v = 0), the magnetic force acting on it is strictly zero.

subtopic: Biomagnetism & Medical Imaging: MRI Technology
question: Which medical imaging technique uses a strong external magnetic field and radiofrequency pulses to produce detailed images of internal soft tissues?
options: X-ray Radiography
Ultrasound Sonography
Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
Positron Emission Tomography (PET)
explanation: MRI scanners use a powerful external magnetic field to align some hydrogen protons in the body’s water and fat. Radiofrequency pulses disturb this alignment. As the protons relax back toward equilibrium, they generate signals that receiver coils detect; the scanner uses these signals and magnetic-field gradients to reconstruct images. MRI does not rely on weak magnetic fields naturally produced by neural ion currents. This is a supplementary medical-physics application and is beyond the core CBSE Class X Science syllabus.
citation: U.S. National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering (NIBIB), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI): https://www.nibib.nih.gov/science-education/science-topics/magnetic-resonance-imaging-mri

Opening a switch so that the circuit carries no current
Operating appliances within the circuit’s rated current capacity
Using a correctly rated fuse in the live conductor
